transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I guess what brings me in is that I recently took on a project for the local historical society, and... I just took it on like I could run the entire fundraiser myself. I was starting all these new quilt designs, calling up volunteers, making schedules, and just... promising deadlines that I couldn't possibly meet. It was just a lot.
During that time, did you find that you needed much less sleep than usual while still feeling full of energy?

Yes, actually. For a while there, I was only sleeping maybe a few hours a night, but I'd wake up completely ready to go. I'd be ready to start sewing or making phone calls right away. But... well, now it's different. Now I either just lie awake at night worrying about everything, or I sleep in late and still feel completely worn out when I finally get up.
About how long did that period of high energy and needing less sleep last?
I'd say it was about five months. That whole overdriven stretch with the historical society project went on for about five months, just going and going, before everything finally fell apart.

No, I haven't experienced anything like that. I just feel exhausted and overwhelmed, but I haven't heard or seen anything unusual.
During this low period, have you had any thoughts that life isn't worth living, or thoughts of hurting yourself?

I don't have a plan to hurt myself, no. But... well, I do catch myself thinking that it would just be easier if I didn't wake up. Sometimes it just feels like it would be better if nobody had to deal with my mess anymore.
How much has this current low period affected your ability to handle everyday tasks, like work, household chores, or taking care of yourself?

Well, it's affected things quite a bit. My husband has had to take over pretty much all the household routines lately. He's also had to step in and deal with the historical society for me, because... well, I just stopped keeping my commitments. I couldn't bring myself to face the people who were waiting on me for things.

Yes, I can still do all that. I mean, I'm still taking showers and brushing my teeth, if that's what you mean. It feels like a lot of effort some days, but I'm still getting dressed and keeping up with my own hygiene. I haven't let that part go.
